Moderation is key. They're supposed to be treats, not a regular part of your daily intake. That's how you end up a Ham with no legs cuz diabetes rotted them off!

Also, the baking at home thing is a great idea. My in laws now make their own cakes, cookies etc at home with reduced or no sugar and they enjoy them just as much.

If anything I think they're nicer as they have more flavour to them than just "ridiculously sweet". They add things like raspberries or blueberries from the garden and nuts for healthy fats.

They have more texture and flavour than any sugar-laden shit you can buy. As a result you naturally eat less as the intensity of flavour and the mouth sensations mean your brain quickly registers that you've eaten. The sugary shit is too easy to mindlessly munch through vast quantities.

Also, when you do decide to have a treat, don't do it while you're watching TV or on the internet. Your brain doesn't pay attention to your food and you don't actually enjoy it, you just automatically keep putting hand to mouth because your focus is elsewhere. You end up overeating and it's usually all the wrong stuff.

If you pay attention to your food and actually savour it then you might find that you don't actually love it as much as you think you do. It's probably just a habit you've formed to snack while you watch TV or whatever. This is especially noticeable once you've cut out the sugary stuff and distracted eating for a while and then decide to have one of your old sugar-bomb "favourites" as a treat.

My father-in-law can't stand some of his old favourites now. He prefers his new diet and he's certainly healthier for it. He's completely reversed all signs of the pre-diabetes as well as lowering his blood pressure and "bad" cholesterol. Type 2 diabetes can be reversed but it's better to change now and prevent it than it is to try and go back once you've already started accumulating the damage to nerves and blood vessels!
